summary: Fetch integer, binary32 and full-group barrier instructions for cooperating threads with separate global and shared storage and checked access bounds; compose instruction segments only after matching their actual program positions.
Derive repeated-barrier ordering and complete memory labels from actual executions; force single-writer publication through the existing memory constraints.
Construct a completed two-thread, two-round computed-publication witness with checked read sources and no circular dependencies; concrete layer ownership, timing and execution proofs remain separate.
remaining: Layer-specific multi-round ownership, timing and admitted execution proofs, launch validation and general barrier forms remain unimplemented. The completed two-round publication witness is not a dense-layer implementation.

from.quote:
Each recorded barrier completion is justified by earlier, actually emitted
arrivals from every participant, with the same CTA, resource, generation and
instruction site. This history property survives arbitrary scheduling and
resource reuse. A memory-ordering certificate uses those arrival positions and
the completion position; it cannot introduce a completion that the machine did
not execute. Memory labels retain their actual address, value, thread and
position. Connecting the certificate to memory constraints is separate from
proving a concrete kernel's write ownership and scratch-storage lifetimes.

A load may use a proposed value. This makes it possible to describe candidate
executions before asking whether PTX's memory rules permit them. A successful
load's address check does not justify its value. The memory graph records every
successful access at its actual position in the execution. Initial contents are
separate writes with no issuing thread. Global and shared locations remain
distinct even when they have the same numeric address. The selected forms are
explicitly relaxed accesses at GPU scope for global storage and CTA scope for
shared storage; the generic word graph represents their common in-scope fragment.

    (atIndex : events[position]? = some (.scalar thread (some space) occ))
    (memory : occ.memory = some effect) :
    ∃ r : Fin (labels program s.global s.shared events).length,

from.quote:
If a location has exactly one program writer, that writer stores before its
arrival, and a consumer loads after the completed barrier, the memory constraints
force the consumer to read that writer. Initialization cannot supply a stale
value. The unique-writer condition includes the entire execution: a later
overwrite would violate it. Fresh scratch for each round makes this a useful
rule for reductions, but a kernel must still prove ownership and timing.

passage.quote:
theorem run_read_from_unique_writer {cfg : Config n} {s : State n} {events : List (Event n)}
    (run : Runs cfg program s events final) (reset : s.barrier = Barrier.reset generation)
    (source co) (phase : History.Phase events)
    (w r : Fin (labels program s.global s.shared events).length) (writer reader : Fin n)
    (valid : Graph.Ordered.Valid (graph program s.global s.shared events source co) (runOrder run reset source co).cross)
    (wo : owner n ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event w) = some writer)
    (ro : owner n ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event r) = some reader)
    (before : ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event w).position <
      History.arrivalPosition (History.completed_arrivals run reset) phase writer)
    (after : phase.position < ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event r).position)
    (written : (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).write w)
    (read : (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).read r)
    (same : (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).sameAddress w r)
    (unique : ∀ v, (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).write v →
      (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).sameAddress v r →
      ¬(graph program s.global s.shared events source co).initial v → v=w) :
    (graph program s.global s.shared events source co).source r=w ∧
      ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event r).effect.value =
      ((graph program s.global s.shared events source co).event w).effect.value :=

from.quote:
A selected software runner reads the current arrays and chooses the checked
binary32 reference result. Its steps are proved to be candidate-machine steps;
this alone does not make the resulting memory graph admissible. A two-thread
witness supplies that additional proof: threads publish inputs, synchronize,
compute sums, publish to fresh locations, synchronize again and store the peer's
result to separate outputs. It works for arbitrary input words, reaches exit in
both threads, and satisfies the original memory constraints. A chronological
certificate also excludes circular dependence through read sources. This is an
existence example, not a restriction on all candidate executions or a full layer
implementation.

theorem admitted_execution (a b : Word) :
    ∃ final events,
      Runs config program (initial a b) events final ∧
      (∀ t, (final.lanes t).halted = true) ∧
      final.global = [a,b,Ptx.Binary32.reference .add b a,Ptx.Binary32.reference .add a b] ∧
      Memory.labels program (initial a b).global (initial a b).shared events = List.ofFn (graph a b).event ∧
      Graph.Ordered.Valid (graph a b) (order a b).cross :=
